titulo: Impression without a click: rewrite the title and description
lead: A page with lots of impressions and few clicks seems to need a new title. Sometimes it does; sometimes the impressions come from people who searched for your brand and clicked the homepage, and the title is not to blame. In this lesson you look at where the impressions come from before changing anything, rewrite only what's worth it, and measure for two weeks.
objetivo: find out where a page's impressions come from before rewriting the title and description, and measure the change for two weeks.

aprende.t: Filter by page and see the queries behind the impressions
When the title isn't the problem
Write a title and description with a specific promise
Measure the change without fooling yourself

hero_alt: Window display of a small shop seen from the sidewalk, with people walking by without going in.

secoes.titulo: Before rewriting, ask where they come from

nos.detalhe: In Performance, sort the pages by impressions and look at the ones with low CTR. The method treats a CTR below 0.5% as a symptom.
Click the page and open the Queries tab. Now you see who saw this result: people searching for your brand or people searching for the topic.
Someone who searched your name saw this page just below the home page and clicked the home page. The title lost nothing. Leave it as it is.
On the second page or beyond, almost no one sees the title. Changing the text doesn't fix it: the problem is authority and content (lesson 8, Plan B).
On the first page, with a topic query and few clicks: that's where the title and description matter. Rewrite with a specific promise and measure for two weeks.

secoes.legenda: Only the last path needs a pen. The others call for patience or another lesson.

texto: List the pages with the most impressions and low CTR over the last 28 days.
Use the non-branded file from lesson 2: it already removes the brand queries.

exemplo.texto: The page /guias/trilha-iniciantes.html had 730 impressions and 4 clicks at position 1.7. The baseline report flagged it as a "quick title win".

texto: Filter by page and read the queries. Add up how much is branded.
If it's almost all branded, the "weak title" diagnosis falls apart.

exemplo.texto: When the page's queries were opened, almost all the impressions came from searches for the brand. The title proposal ended up light: say what the page is, for when topic searches show up. It stayed as a draft, with no result measurement.

texto: Title: what the person gets, with a number or a concrete scope, in about 60 characters or fewer. Description: what's on the page, in one or two sentences.
Don't promise what the page doesn't deliver.
Note the date of the change, the CTR and the position from before. Wait two weeks before judging or changing again.
If your position changed a lot during the period, the CTR comparison isn't valid.

Made-up example from a ceramics shop: the new title says what the person gets and the angle.

• Changing the title of a page that only shows up for the brand: it changes nothing.
  • Changing it again after 3 days: there's no time to measure.
  • Clickbait title: the click goes back to Google and the page loses.

secoes.titulo: Practice: one swap with a diagnosis
secoes.sub: E2 asks for a two-week wait.

exercicios.texto: Pick 3 pages with impressions and low CTR. For each one, open the queries and classify them: branded, non-branded far, non-branded close.
exercicios.pronto: each of the 3 pages has its classification and its 3 queries with the most impressions noted down.

exercicios.texto: On the "non-branded, close" page (if there is one), rewrite the title and description and fill in the log. Two weeks later, complete the "after" column.
exercicios.pronto: the log has the swap date, before and after numbers, and a written decision; or one sentence saying why none of the 3 needed a swap.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: A page has 730 impressions and 4 clicks at position 1.7. What is the first step?
opcoes: Open the page's queries and check whether the impressions are branded or topic-based.
perguntas.explica: At INEMA, the weak-title suspicion fell apart when the queries showed the impressions came from searches for the brand.

perguntas.p: The page's queries are topic-based, but the position is 38. Does changing the title fix it?
opcoes: No: at position 38 almost nobody sees the title; the problem is authority and content.
Yes, if it has an emoji.
perguntas.explica: The title matters on the first page. Further down, the way forward is Plan B from lesson 8: backlinks and sections for the queries that showed up.

perguntas.p: You changed the title 3 days ago and the CTR hasn't moved. What should you do?
opcoes: Wait the full two weeks, with a stable position, before judging.
Go back to the old one.
perguntas.explica: Two weeks is the minimum for the measurement. Changing earlier mixes both titles into the same number.

perguntas.p: What makes a title good for the person searching?
opcoes: A specific, true promise: what the person gets and the angle.
perguntas.explica: A clickbait title wins the click and loses the person right after. A specific promise that is kept is what holds them.

itens.texto: See where the impressions come from before you rewrite.
Title matters near the top; far from it, the problem is something else.
With an AI summary on the page, studies measure fewer clicks (Pew, 2025: 8% versus 15% without a summary). A lower CTR is not always a bad title.
